HTTP and WebSocket server with request parsing, response staging, and connection management.

# Purpose
This C file implements the main logic for an HTTP server that also supports WebSocket connections. It defines the server object lifecycle functions [`fd_http_server_new`](<#fd_http_server_new>), [`fd_http_server_join`](<#fd_http_server_join>), [`fd_http_server_leave`](<#fd_http_server_leave>), and [`fd_http_server_delete`](<#fd_http_server_delete>), plus the socket setup function [`fd_http_server_listen`](<#fd_http_server_listen>) and the event loop entry point [`fd_http_server_poll`](<#fd_http_server_poll>). The server uses `poll(2)` to manage one listening socket, normal HTTP connections, and WebSocket connections in the same loop. It also defines helper functions that convert close reasons and HTTP methods to strings.

The file contains the full request and response handling path. It parses HTTP requests with `picohttpparser`, checks request method, path, and headers, and calls user callbacks through `fd_http_server_callbacks_t` to build responses. It also handles WebSocket upgrade requests, frame parsing, ping and pong frames, message delivery, and outgoing frame queues. The code uses pool and treap templates to manage connection slots and to track connections that hold buffered response data. It also includes optional Zstandard compression support for WebSocket messages when `FD_HAS_ZSTD` is enabled, and it provides staging helpers such as [`fd_http_server_printf`](<#fd_http_server_printf>), [`fd_http_server_memcpy`](<#fd_http_server_memcpy>), [`fd_http_server_stage_body`](<#fd_http_server_stage_body>), and [`fd_http_server_ws_send`](<#fd_http_server_ws_send>) for building response bodies and WebSocket payloads in the server buffer.
